extracted.intended_audience: multimodal ML researchers, dataset creators, and annotators working on video question answering (particularly humor/creative/magic video QA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for constructing and annotating FunQA — a visual-centric VideoQA dataset (HumorQA, CreativeQA, MagicQA) focused on counter-intuitive and spatial-temporal reasoning. Covers video selection, annotator training/qualification, annotation formats, quality control, language augmentation, and automated/human evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction principles
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA adhered to three principles: our dataset is visual centered and emphasizes counter-intuitive reasoning, spatial-temporal reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles guide video selection and dataset design; the collection comprises 4,365 videos split into HumorQA, CreativeQA, and MagicQA to specifically stress vision-centric and counter-intuitive tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-tolerance offensive-content policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a zero-tolerance policy regarding the inclusion of offensive content in our dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During video sourcing (selection and clipping) and annotation stages, ensure offensive content is completely eliminated via rigorous training, strict reviewer checks, and multi-round reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: HumorQA subset selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: HumorQA is visual-centered, emphasizes counter-intuitive reasoning, and contains short clips (average length 7s) where understanding humor requires holistic understanding plus common sense (humor arises from incongruity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select short everyday-life clips whose humor stems from juxtaposition/violation of expectations; use these to challenge models' integration and deep reasoning abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CreativeQA subset selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: CreativeQA (from Kasou Taishou) consists of longer skit/performance videos emphasizing originality and imitation, testing information integration and spatial-temporal comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performance/imitation videos that require understanding creative intent, props, and longer temporal sequences (avg 48s) to challenge extraction of creative and temporal cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: MagicQA subset selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: MagicQA contains magic performance videos across genres whose essence is creating seemingly impossible illusions (disappearance, creation, transformation) with abundant spatial-temporal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select magic clips where models must track object changes and infer underlying mechanics; note that annotators are typically not professional magicians so method annotations are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video clip selection & clipping principle
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA Video Selection and Clip Principle: select and clip videos such that they fit the dataset principles and exclude sensitive/offensive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators were trained and qualified to produce high-quality clips; clips sourced from platforms and TV episodes; follow provided principles/figures (Fig. A2) and eliminate offensive material at both selection and clip stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotator pre-processing & qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotators downloaded videos and underwent rigorous training; only annotators who successfully completed the Clip task according to requirements were considered qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide systematic training for each task type; qualification gates ensure only trained annotators proceed to annotation stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive Timestamp Localization Task (format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotation format is a pair of numbers enclosed in square brackets, [xxxx, xxxx]; annotators record the time intervals in which they felt pleasure (amusement or shock) while watching the video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record precise intervals (frames/seconds) corresponding to the counter-intuitive moment(s). Note: models currently fail to perform this task reliably (no model can answer timestamp localization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Detailed Description Task (H2/C2/M2) — 'what you see is what you get'
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide objective descriptions of what happened in the selected interval, emphasizing a 'what you see is what you get' approach; annotations should only cover the selected time intervals and should not include subjective adverbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid subjective adverbs (e.g., 'vividly'); be concise when describing characters/objects and add modifiers if ambiguous (bad example: 'a man and a woman'; better: 'a man wearing a red hat and a woman wearing an apron').

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitiveness Reasoning Task (H3/C3/M3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the video is interesting (counter-intuitive) in the context of the overall content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires interpretive answers based on analysis, reasoning, and prior knowledge — i.e., explain the incongruity, violation of expectation, or why an event is surprising/funny given normal expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magic Method Task (M4) annotation constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: M4 asks about magic methods, but annotators are not professional magicians and it is difficult to provide complete annotations for magic methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a small number of examples were provided for M4 and these do not appear in the released FunQA dataset; treat M4 as a limited/example-only task rather than a broadly annotated label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation coverage constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations should only cover the selected time intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asked to describe/explain, do not include content outside the [xxxx, xxxx] interval; remain focused on the chosen clip segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-person, multi-round quality review
rubrics_metrics.description: Every annotation included in the final release underwent rigorous multi-person, multi-round review processes; each released annotation was scrutinized by three distinct annotators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-time quality reviews check adherence to requirements, removal of sensitive content, and textual sensitivity; a consensus evaluation study sampled 10% of videos for annotator consistency scoring (high/medium/low between first and second annotations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language augmentation & translation pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: For each QA pair, GPT-3.5 was used to translate Chinese answers into English and to generate five synonymous sentences; incorrect/incomplete generations were filtered out and hand-corrected for cultural/idiomatic mismatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a carefully designed GPT-3.5 prompt (Fig. A4) and manually screen outputs (e.g., Fig. A5) for Chinese-English cultural differences, especially for titles; filter or manually edit ambiguous/incorrect translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright & privacy handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect copyright and personal identity information; the release supplies only YouTube video IDs rather than original raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distribute raw videos; remove personally identifying or offensive content during review; follow prior practices (e.g., Kinetics) to share IDs only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task taxonomy and expected outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tasks: H2/C2/M2 = Detailed video description (free-text); H3/C3/M3 = Counter-intuitiveness reasoning (free-text); H4/C4 = Title generation; C5 = creativity scoring (numeric). FunQA also provides Multi-choice (FunQA-MC) and Dialog (FunQA-DIA) variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions and explanations are free-text; FunQA-MC contains multiple-choice description questions; FunQA-DIA converts QA pairs into dialogues using GPT-3.5 for LLM-friendly formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics used
rubrics_metrics.description: Use traditional NLG metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr), representation-based metric (BLEURT), WUPS, and a GPT-4 based metric; C5 (creativity) evaluated by accuracy between predicted score and official score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand strengths/limits: BLEU/ROUGE/CIDEr measure n-gram/overlap and have brevity/TF-IDF considerations; BLEURT captures semantic similarity via pre-trained models; WUPS has severe limitations for phrases and certain word pairs; GPT-4 based metric uses prompt-engineered semantic evaluation and can better handle logic/semantics but may be unstable across runs (average multiple evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: GPT-4 prompt design areas for automatic scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: GPT-4 prompts were crafted to score tasks across multiple specific areas: for Description evaluation — text length, text content variation, text detail variation, logical text description, and linguistic ability; for Counter-intuitiveness Reasoning — expressiveness of language, logic of response, common sense of response, understanding of counter-intuition, differences in text detail, and length of text; for Title evaluation — use description, comprehension, and title as references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the reference annotation and model output to GPT-4 per prompt (Fig. A11–A13); because GPT-4 evaluations can vary, run multiple evaluations and average when necessary to mitigate instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timestamp Localization task known failure mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Current models fail to perform Timestamp Localization Task: models tend to describe content rather than output specific frame/second intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect this task to remain unsolved by existing VLMs; treat timestamp localization as a hard benchmark for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio ablation / visual-centric emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: FunQA is designed to emphasize understanding of 'fun' primarily through visual aspects; ablation experiments muting audio showed traditional metrics remained basically unchanged and GPT-4 scores fluctuated little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluation should prioritize visual inputs; audio may be retained but is not expected to substantially ease benchmark challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: FunQA extension generation protocols (MC/DIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use GPT-3.5 system prompts to convert descriptions/explanations into multi-choice questions (FunQA-MC) or into dialogues with added context and future dialogue development (FunQA-DIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter and validate GPT-3.5 outputs; FunQA-MC-R is a multi-choice subset specifically containing counter-intuitive reasoning questions sampled from Task 2.
